dao_vote/VoteDatum.title: VoteDatum
dao_vote/VoteDatum.description:
Token-Weighted DAO Voting (Mint-Lock-Vote)

 Users lock governance tokens at this script address to cast votes
 on proposals. Each governance token locked equals one vote.
 Voting weight is determined by the quantity of governance tokens
 in the UTxO — no separate weight field needed.

 Flow:
   1. Voter sends governance tokens + datum to script address (creates vote)
   2. Anyone can read the script UTxOs off-chain to tally votes
   3. After the voting deadline, voter reclaims their tokens (Unlock)

 Parameterized by:
   - gov_token_policy: governance token policy ID
   - gov_token_name: governance token asset name
   - voting_deadline: POSIX time after which votes can be unlocked

fields.description: Proposal number being voted on

fields.title: vote_for
fields.description: True = yes, False = no

anyOf.description: Voter reclaims governance tokens after voting period ends

anyOf.description: Owner extends the deadline by checking in

anyOf.description: Beneficiary claims after deadline has passed

dead_mans_switch/SwitchDatum.title: SwitchDatum
dead_mans_switch/SwitchDatum.description:
Dead Man's Switch / Inheritance Validator

 Owner must periodically "check in" to prove they are still active.
 If the owner fails to check in before the deadline, the beneficiary
 can claim the funds. The owner always retains full withdrawal rights.

fields.title: check_in_deadline

fields.title: check_in_interval
fields.description: Milliseconds between required check-ins

dutch_auction/AuctionDatum.title: AuctionDatum
dutch_auction/AuctionDatum.description:
Dutch Auction Validator

 Price starts high and decreases linearly over time until someone buys
 or the auction expires at the reserve price. The seller locks an item
 at the script address. Buyers purchase at the current (decaying) price.
 The seller can cancel and reclaim at any time.

fields.title: decay_per_ms
fields.description: Lovelace decrease per millisecond

anyOf.description: Buyer purchases at the computed price

anyOf.title: Cancel
anyOf.description: Seller cancels the auction

governance_propose/ProposeRedeemer.title: ProposeRedeemer
governance_propose/ProposeRedeemer.description:
Treasury Withdrawal Guardrail — Propose Handler

 A governance guardrail script that only permits TreasuryWithdrawal proposals.
 Enforces:
   - Governance action must be TreasuryWithdrawal
   - Deposit must meet minimum threshold (100 ADA)
   - Transaction must be signed by the authorized proposer

governance_publish/Action.title: Action
governance_publish/Action.description:
DRep Registration Controller

 Controls who can register, update, or unregister as a Delegate Representative
 (DRep) on Cardano's governance system. Only the designated admin can perform
 DRep operations through this script.

 This publish handler rejects any certificate that isn't a DRep operation,
 ensuring the script is narrowly scoped to its intended purpose.

governance_vote/VoteRedeemer.title: VoteRedeemer
governance_vote/VoteRedeemer.description:
SPO Governance Vote Validator

 Ensures that governance votes cast on behalf of a stake pool
 are authorized by the pool operator. Parameterized by the
 operator's verification key hash.

 In Cardano's Conway governance, SPOs can vote on certain
 governance actions. This validator gates that ability behind
 a transaction signature from the pool operator.

anyOf.title: CastVote
anyOf.description: Cast votes — operator must sign

multi_beneficiary/InheritanceDatum.title: InheritanceDatum
multi_beneficiary/InheritanceDatum.description:
Multi-Beneficiary Inheritance Vault

 Models a fund-splitting pattern where an owner locks ADA that can be
 distributed to multiple heirs after a specified time. Each beneficiary
 receives a share defined in basis points (10000 = 100%).

 The owner can withdraw everything at any time. Beneficiaries can only
 claim their individual shares after the unlock time has passed.

fields.description:
List of (beneficiary_key_hash, share_bps) pairs
 share_bps is in basis points: 10000 = 100%

fields.title: unlock_after
fields.description: POSIX time after which beneficiaries can claim

anyOf.title: OwnerWithdraw
anyOf.description: Owner takes everything — no time restriction

anyOf.title: ClaimShare
anyOf.description: A beneficiary claims their share

reference_scripts/RegistryDatum.title: RegistryDatum
reference_scripts/RegistryDatum.description:
CIP-33 Reference Scripts Pattern

 Demonstrates two validators working together:
 1. script_registry (spend) — admin-controlled registry for storing reference scripts
 2. script_user (spend) — a vault that verifies a reference script is available

 Key CIP-33 concept: Reference scripts allow transactions to reference a script
 stored in an existing UTxO rather than including the full script in the witness
 set. This reduces transaction size and fees for commonly-used scripts.

 The registry stores scripts as reference_script on its UTxO outputs.
 The user validator checks tx.reference_inputs to verify a script is available.
 Registry datum — tracks the admin, stored script hash, and version.

fields.title: admin
fields.description: Admin's verification key hash (authorized to update/remove)

fields.title: script_hash
fields.description: Hash of the stored reference script

fields.title: version
fields.description: Version number — incremented on each update

tagged_output/TaggedDatum.title: TaggedDatum
tagged_output/TaggedDatum.description:
Tagged Output — Double Satisfaction Prevention

 Problem: Multiple script inputs could be satisfied by a single output
          (double satisfaction attack).
 Solution: Tag each output with the hash of its corresponding input's
           output reference. Each input verifies its unique tag exists.

fields.title: input_tag
fields.description: blake2b_256 hash of the input's OutputReference (unique tag)

utxo_indexer/TokenDatum.title: TokenDatum
utxo_indexer/TokenDatum.description:
UTxO Indexing — O(1) Input-to-Output Linking

 Problem: Linking specific inputs to specific outputs requires iterating.
          This is O(n) and opens double satisfaction attacks.
 Solution: Redeemer carries indices pointing directly to the relevant
           input and output. Validator verifies the index is correct.
